title: Synapse warehouse to Fabric Warehouse
summary: Design a dedicated SQL pool (distributions, partitions, CTAS), load it with a pipeline and stored procedures, trace the lineage, check the star, then port it to Fabric Warehouse.
story: Contoso's warehouse runs on an **Azure Synapse dedicated SQL pool**. Management wants to move to **Microsoft Fabric Warehouse** next year; until then, the reports must stay right and fast.

You take over the pool's physical design (distributions, replicated tables, partitions, CTAS), the daily load by a Synapse pipeline that calls a stored procedure, the documentation (column lineage, star model checks), then you port a table to Fabric Warehouse and note what changes.

T-SQL is translated for a documented subset and the data statements really run on DuckDB; distributions, partitions and data movement are a teaching model, not Synapse or Fabric telemetry. Nothing connects to Azure.
goals: Choose a distribution (REPLICATE, HASH, ROUND_ROBIN) and read the data movement of a plan
Partition a fact table so that the pool skips partitions
Load a warehouse with a Synapse pipeline that calls a stored procedure with typed parameters
Trace a column's lineage and check a star model
Port a table from the dedicated pool to Fabric Warehouse

steps.title: Load bronze
instructions: The Synapse pipeline of step 6 starts from `bronze.orders`. Open `projects/synapse-to-fabric/load_bronze.sql` and click **Run active SQL** in Mosaic: it copies the 12 raw orders of `source.orders`.

steps.title: Distribute the star in the dedicated pool
instructions: Open `factory/sql/pool/01_star_schema.sql` (created by **Create lab files**). In **Cloud Lab › SQL pool**, keep Synapse, choose this script, then **Run script**.

Read the tables panel: `dim_segment` is replicated on every node, `fact_orders` is hash-distributed on `order_id`, and `fact_orders_by_customer` shows a skewed distribution (one corporate account dominates). Also look at the data movement (shuffle, broadcast) of the queries.

checks.label: 01_star_schema.sql ran without error on the Synapse pool
dbo.fact_orders is hash-distributed on order_id (simulated model)

steps.title: Practice: a distribution key without skew
instructions: Do the exercise **Choose a distribution column without skew**: the hash column must have many distinct values, few NULLs, and serve the joins.

steps.title: Partition the sales by month
instructions: Open `factory/sql/pool/02_partitions.sql`, then **Run script** (Synapse). The `fact_sales_2026` table has one partition per month (RANGE RIGHT).
Compare the two queries: filtering with `YEAR(order_date)` reads every partition, filtering on `order_date` itself reads only one. The script then loads a month with a partition switch (SWITCH).

checks.label: 02_partitions.sql ran without error on the Synapse pool

steps.title: A stored procedure you can run again
instructions: Open `factory/sql/pool/03_procedures.sql`, then **Run script** (Synapse). The `dbo.usp_segment_revenue` procedure rebuilds its table with a CTAS next to the old one, then swaps it in with `RENAME OBJECT`: readers never see an empty table, and running it again is safe.

checks.label: 03_procedures.sql ran without error on the Synapse pool
The procedure produced dbo.segment_revenue (warehouse.segment_revenue in the catalog)

steps.title: Load gold with a Synapse pipeline
instructions: The `pl_sqlpool_daily` pipeline (Synapse) stages the orders with a CTAS, rebuilds silver, then calls the stored procedure `warehouse.usp_load_gold_revenue` with typed parameters.
1. In **Cloud Lab › Pipelines**, choose Synapse and `pl_sqlpool_daily`, then **Run on local lakehouse**. Look at the output of `Check gold`: the **Public Sector** segment is missing.

2. Find out why in `factory/synapse/pipeline/pl_sqlpool_daily.json`: the procedure keeps the segments with at least `min_orders` orders, and the pipeline passes `"2"` (Int32). Change it to `"1"`, then run again.
The orchestration is simulated; the CTAS, the scripts and the procedure really run on the local catalog.

checks.label: A local run of pl_sqlpool_daily (Synapse) succeeded up to Check gold
gold.revenue_by_segment holds the 4 segments, Public Sector included
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS segments, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE segment_name = 'Public Sector') AS public_sector FROM gold.revenue_by_segment

steps.title: Practice: call a procedure with typed parameters
instructions: Do the exercise **Call a SQL pool procedure with typed parameters**: the stored procedure activity of a Synapse pipeline, its parameters and their types.

steps.title: Add the margin and trace its lineage
instructions: Finance wants the margin on each sales line. In **BI Lab** (**Create lab files** if needed), open `bi/warehouse/05_fct_sales.sql` and add this column to `gold.fct_sales`:
l.quantity * l.unit_price - l.discount_amount - l.quantity * dp.unit_cost AS margin_amount
Click **Build warehouse**, then open the **Lineage** tab and choose `gold.fct_sales` › `margin_amount`: it goes back to the shop's order lines **and** to the ERP's unit cost, through `dim_product`.
Lineage is a static analysis of the SQL (sqlglot): it runs nothing, it reads the text of the scripts.

checks.label: The lineage of gold.fct_sales.margin_amount goes back to the order lines and the ERP cost

steps.title: Check the star model
instructions: Open the **Star model** tab of the BI Lab (after **Build warehouse** or **Analyze only**). The `bi/model.json` file declares the facts, the dimensions, their keys, their grain and their relationships (cardinality, cross-filter, active relationship).
Every check must be green: unique keys, unknown member, grain, SCD2 validity, relationships, a single active relationship per path. Read why the ship date is an **inactive** relationship.

checks.label: Every star model check is green, with both facts

steps.title: Port a table to Fabric Warehouse
instructions: Open `projects/synapse-to-fabric/port_to_fabric.sql`. In **Cloud Lab › SQL pool**, choose **Fabric Warehouse**, then **Run active .sql**: Fabric refuses `DISTRIBUTION` and indexes, which it manages itself.

Port the script: replace the options with `WITH ( CLUSTER BY (order_date) )`, `NVARCHAR` with `VARCHAR` (Fabric strings are UTF-8) and `MONEY` with `DECIMAL(19, 4)`. Run it again: the table must give the same revenue (4,985) over the 4 segments.

checks.label: port_to_fabric.sql ran without error on Fabric Warehouse
dbo.fact_daily_revenue_fw is managed by Fabric (AUTO distribution, simulated model)
Same result as before the port: 4 segments, 4,985
checks.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT segment_id) AS segments, ROUND(SUM(revenue), 2) AS revenue FROM warehouse.fact_daily_revenue_fw

steps.title: Practice: port a pool table to Fabric
instructions: Do the exercise **Port a dedicated pool table to Fabric Warehouse**. Its starter script is refused by Fabric on purpose: fix it.

steps.title: Write the migration checklist
instructions: Complete `projects/synapse-to-fabric/MIGRATION.md`: physical design, types and constraints, loading, governance.
This step cannot be checked automatically: tick it yourself when the checklist is written.
